ai.title: Overhaul SDK example 2 to show custom agents and tools
ai.summary: sdk/README.md Example 2 now uses `AgentDefinition` and `getCustomToolDefinition` for a sentiment analyzer agent with a `fetch_api_data` tool. The previous image analysis example using `generateInitialRunState` and `withAdditionalMessage` is removed. The tool handler now returns a structured JSON array instead of a `toolResultMessage` string.

eli5.text: The documentation example that shows up in the software development kit has been rewritten to focus on custom agents and tools instead of image analysis. If you looked at the example, you would see a sentiment analyzer agent that uses a fetch_api_data tool, and the tool now returns structured JSON data rather than plain text messages. This change is live today in the SDK documentation and affects developers using the example code.

ai.title: Fix SDK README agent config references
ai.summary: Updated `sdk/README.md` to correct terminology for agent configuration. Changed references from 'agent config' to 'agent definition' and updated the expected type from `AgentConfig` to `AgentDefinition` for the `agentDefinitions` parameter. This aligns the documentation with the actual SDK types.

eli5.text: The help guide inside the software development kit now uses the correct name for a set of instructions you give to an automated helper. Where it used to say you were handing over an 'agent config' that must follow the 'AgentConfig' format, it now says 'agent definition' following the 'AgentDefinition' format, and it mentions you pass these instructions through a specific setting. If you read that guide to learn how to customize the helper, the words now match the actual options the software recognizes.

ai.title: SDK version bump 0.1.29
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk from 0.1.28 to 0.1.29 in sdk/package.json. Internal release cycle update. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: The package that developer tools use to talk to Codebuff got a routine internal version bump, like a car getting a scheduled service with no new features. If you use Codebuff's developer SDK, you won't see any difference in how your tools behave because nothing functionally changed. This just keeps the internal release cycle on track for the team maintaining it.

ai.title: Move finish event to backend websocket
ai.summary: The 'finish' response-chunk is now sent from backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts instead of being printed locally by npm-app/src/cli.ts. This centralizes the termination signal for agent sessions. The CLI no longer emits PrintModeFinish objects to stdout, relying on the websocket stream for cost and agent metadata.

eli5.text: When you run a coding assistant session that connects to a backend server, the final summary showing how much it cost and which assistant did the work now arrives through the live data feed that streams between your computer and the service, instead of being printed directly by your local application. You won't see a difference in what's displayed, but the signal that tells everything the session is complete now travels through the same stream as all the other live updates, which centralizes how agent sessions end and report their cost and identity. This affects anyone running a coding assistant session against the hosted backend and is live today.

ai.title: Add print mode start event
ai.summary: Added `printModeStartSchema` to `common/src/types/print-mode.ts` and emitted a `response-chunk` with type `start` in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` before `mainPrompt`. This signals the beginning of a print-mode response stream, carrying optional `agentId`. Scope limited to backend websocket handler and common type definitions.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant in print mode, the stream now announces that it's starting before it begins sending any text or tool activity, optionally including which agent is responding. If you were watching the real-time feed of responses, you'd see a clear 'start' marker appear at the very beginning of each print-mode reply, rather than the first chunk arriving without any preamble. The change is limited to the backend websocket handler and the shared type definitions that describe the different kinds of events the stream can emit.

ai.title: Release 1.0.475 version bump in npm-app release package
ai.summary: The codebuff release package version field in npm-app/release/package.json was bumped from 1.0.474 to 1.0.475 as part of the Freebuff monorepo's internal release cycle. This is a pure version increment with no source code changes in this commit (stats +1/-1), serving as the packaging marker for the accumulated release updates below. The bump aggregates the user-facing changes shipped since 1.0.474 per the release instructions. Consumers resolving the codebuff package will pull this new release version from the npm registry.
ai.evidence: npm-app/release/package.json hunk changes the codebuff package version field from 1.0.474 to 1.0.475 (single line edit in the version property of the release manifest).

eli5.text: This release routes all Gemini AI model calls through OpenRouter, so you can use the latest Gemini models with a unified access method and updated model naming. The CLI no longer prints finish notifications to your terminal directly, instead getting them through the backend websocket for cleaner output. A new start event now signals the beginning of agent responses over the websocket, giving better feedback when an agent starts working. The SDK documentation was rewritten with a new example showing how to connect a custom-built agent and a custom tool, plus clearer instructions for first-run setup. The SDK package itself was bumped to version 0.1.29 and the Google Generative AI API key was removed from internal settings to simplify configuration. Upgrading gives you access to newer Gemini models through the improved routing, cleaner terminal behavior, and an easier SDK getting-started experience.

ai.title: Eval judge and runner switch Gemini models to OpenRouter
ai.summary: Eval pipeline updates `judge-git-eval.ts`, `post-eval-analysis.ts`, and `run-git-evals.ts` to use `models.openrouter_gemini2_5_pro_preview` and `models.openrouter_gemini2_5_flash` instead of direct `geminiModels` constants. Imports shift from `geminiModels` to `models` from `@codebuff/common/old-constants`. Routing eval traffic through OpenRouter likely addresses upstream availability or quota constraints.

eli5.text: If you ran one of the internal test runs that automatically grades how well our coding assistant performs, that test will now route its questions through a different gateway to reach the same Gemini models. This only affects the automated quality-check system used by people building the assistant; you, as a user, would not notice anything different. The change is already live in the internal test software today. The switch was made because this gateway helps avoid the upstream availability and quota limits that were causing the test runs to stall, as recorded in the change history from September 6, 2025.

ai.title: Add read-only-commander agent for terminal commands
ai.summary: New `read-only-commander` agent added to base2 spawnable list. Uses `x-ai/grok-code-fast-1` model. Restricted to read-only terminal commands via explicit system prompt constraints. `scout` agent gains `code_search` tool and updated prompts. `x-ai/grok-code-fast-1` added to `ModelName` type union in `agent-definition.ts`.

eli5.text: The coding assistant can now hand off quick, read-only terminal checks to a new specialized helper, so it can peek at your project's structure or search code without touching anything. You wouldn't run or install anything different yourself; when the assistant needs a fast fact about your codebase, it may now spawn this helper instead of doing the work directly. The main assistant and its scouting helper also received minor prompt updates and an additional search capability. This behavior is available as of the September 6, 2025 snapshot.

ai.title: AgentDefinition handleSteps toolResult type update
ai.summary: The handleSteps callback in AgentDefinition now types toolResult as ToolResultOutput[] | undefined instead of string | undefined. This aligns the agent definition interface with structured tool outputs from content-part. The change is scoped to common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts.

eli5.text: An internal building block that the assistant uses to understand the results of its tool calls was tightened up so it now expects the richer, structured results the assistant actually receives at runtime, instead of a loose string. This is behind-the-scenes refinement that aligns the code's expectations with how the assistant works, not something you will see change in conversations.

ai.title: Add grok-code-fast-1 model and update agent README
ai.summary: Added x-ai/grok-code-fast-1 to ModelName union in agent-definition.ts. Updated toolResult type from string to ToolResultOutput[]. Restructured .agents/README.md and initial-agents-dir/README.md to move Getting Started and Need Help sections to top.

eli5.text: The guide at the top of your agent folder now leads with how to get started and get help, instead of burying those steps under a file list. When you read the agent guide, you'll immediately see the steps to edit, test, and publish your first agent. Behind the scenes, the system can now recognize one more AI model named grok-code-fast-1, and the way tool results are passed between steps has been made more precise, though you won't see that part unless you're building agents yourself.

ai.title: Merge agent type definitions into util-types
ai.summary: Consolidated scattered agent type files into a single `util-types.ts` module. Deleted `codebuff-message.ts`, `content-part.ts`, `data-content.ts`, `json.ts`, and `provider-metadata.ts`, moving their exports into the new file. Updated imports in `agent-definition.ts`, `tools.ts`, and `context-pruner.ts` to reference `util-types`. This reduces file fragmentation in the agent type system.

eli5.text: The program's internal address book for how the assistant reads and understands messages was cleaned up so all the related definitions now live in one place instead of being spread across several files. If you looked behind the scenes you'd see the old separate pages for messages, images, and tool data were folded into a single reference sheet, and any code that used to fetch from the old pages was quietly redirected to the new one with no change to what you actually see. The change is live today and only touches how the system organizes itself internally.

ai.title: Accumulate edit tool results across agent steps
ai.summary: Editor logic in `.agents/base2/editor.ts` now accumulates `write_file` and `str_replace` results incrementally via `getLatestEditToolResults` instead of filtering only the final `agentState.messageHistory`. This fixes a bug where edits from earlier steps were lost if the history was truncated or overwritten. Scope is limited to the internal agent editor. New helper function extracts tool messages following the last assistant turn per step.

eli5.text: When you run an agentic task that edits files across multiple steps, the final report now collects every edit result from every step instead of only the ones still sitting in the most recent conversation slice. In practice, if the conversation history got trimmed or rewritten mid-run, earlier edit results would previously disappear from the summary; now they're kept, so you see the full list of files actually written or changed. Only edit tools that succeeded are included, and only tool messages that came after the last assistant message in each step are accumulated. This affects any run using the internal agent editor today.
